events.title: TypeScript preview released
events.summary: Microsoft released the TypeScript preview on October 1, 2012 — a typed superset of JavaScript by Anders Hejlsberg.
events.about: TypeScript adds optional static types, interfaces, and generics to JavaScript, then compiles to plain JS. It powers large frontends (Angular, VS Code itself) and Node backends where teams want compile-time checks without leaving the JS ecosystem. `.ts` files catch typos before runtime and enable IDE autocomplete at scale.

narrative.whyChosen: TypeScript became the default for large-scale JavaScript applications and framework tooling.
narrative.whyImportant: It bridged JavaScript's flexibility with IDE support and refactoring safety enterprise teams expected.
narrative.problemSolved: Plain JavaScript lacked types for million-line codebases; teams needed safety without abandoning the web platform.
